item.title: Xi urges steady course for ties
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-25
Xi urges steady course for ties At welcoming ceremony, he calls on China, US to strengthen communication, cooperate with sincerity and coexist in peace President Xi Jinping has underlined the need for China and the US to strengthen communication, cooperate with sincerity and coexist in peace, saying that achieving the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation and "making America great again" can go hand in hand. Xi, who is paying a state visit to the US, made the remarks on Thursday in Washington in a speech delivered at the welcoming ceremony hosted by US President Donald Trump at the White House. "I'm visiting the United States at the invitation of President Trump to carry on our friendship, expand cooperation and promote the well-being of both our peoples," he said in the speech. Xi noted that his agreement with Trump, reached during the US president's visit to China in May, on building a constructive China-US relationship of strategic stability has been widely welcomed by the people of the two countries and the international community. "China and the US are different in national conditions, but through candid, in-depth and continued dialogue, our two countries can understand each other better, seek common ground while shelving differences, and build up mutual trust," he said. Xi pointed out that the interests of the two countries are deeply intertwined, and there is plenty of room for them to work together. "China-US cooperation may not solve every problem in the world, but without cooperation, it would be hard to solve many of the world's problems," he said. Xi expressed the hope that Chinese companies will be treated fairly in the US, saying that "working together, we can lengthen the list of cooperation and shorten the list of issues". Noting that both China and the US are leading nations in artificial intelligence, he said that both countries have the capability and responsibility to develop and manage AI for good, and to ensure that the development of AI is always under human control and serves the well-being of the people. Xi reiterated that China and the US, as two major countries, stand to gain from cooperation and will both lose in confrontation. "We do not need to avoid mentioning competition, but our competition should be a healthy one and should be kept within bounds. It should be a race of catching up with each other, not a wrestle in which one either wins or loses," he said. "China and the United States must hold the line of no conflict and no confrontation between us. And we can certainly find the right path for two great countries to get along on this planet." He said that the two militaries should maintain regular dialogue and improve mechanisms for crisis communication and prevention. In his speech, Xi announced an invitation for 100,000 young Americans to visit China for exchanges and studies in the coming five years, and said two pandas will come to their new home in Zoo Atlanta and meet with the American people. Addressing the ceremony, Trump said that from the time of his first election in 2016, he has forged a friendship with Xi, which he described as "a truly great friendship actually built on mutual respect and the vital interests of our people". Planeside welcome On Wednesday, President Xi and his wife, Peng Liyuan, were warmly greeted by President Trump and his wife, Melania Trump, in a rare planeside welcome at Joint Base Andrews outside Washington, DC, as Xi began his first state visit to the US in 11 years. American children presented bouquets of flowers to Xi and Peng upon their arrival. Honor guards lined both sides of the red carpet in salute. The welcoming ceremony also included a 21-gun salute, the playing of the national anthems of both countries, and a military flyover. The gesture was notable even by broader diplomatic standards, and the arrangement was described by US media as a "rare" and "unusual" departure from protocol, as US presidents typically receive visiting foreign leaders at the White House rather than greeting them at the airport. Robert Lawrence Kuhn, a US scholar and longtime observer of China, emphasized the message conveyed by the summit itself. "The meeting itself is the biggest announcement: Both leaders are committed to a stable relationship," Kuhn said. "It's a dangerously different world in which we're living. This is especially why stable US-China relations are critical: to keep the world from getting any worse." A more stable relationship would also benefit the US economy, in which private businesses are particularly sensitive to instability and uncertainty, he added. He also called for practical China-US cooperation in areas including combating drug trafficking and addressing artificial intelligence risks. Suisheng Zhao, a professor and director of the Center for China-US Cooperation at the University of Denver's Josef Korbel School of Global and Public Affairs, said he expected the immediate focus to be on limited agreements on specific issues, including a trade-war truce, rare earth export controls and agricultural trade.

item.title: UK returns 12 cultural relics and artworks to China
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-25
12 cultural relics and artworks seized by UK police returned to China Share - WeChat
Twelve cultural relics and artworks seized by London's Metropolitan Police during investigations were returned to China at a handover ceremony at China's UK embassy on Wednesday. Mark Gooding, director Asia Pacific at Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office of the UK, said at the ceremony that cultural heritage forms part of our shared human story, and that preserving it for future generations is a responsibility that transcends borders and politics. (Reporters: He Xiating and Zheng Wanyin)

item.title: Chinese, US first ladies visit National Museum of Asian Art
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-25
Chinese, US first ladies visit National Museum of Asian Art WASHINGTON -- Peng Liyuan, wife of Chinese President Xi Jinping, and Melania Trump, wife of US President Donald Trump, visited the National Museum of Asian Art in Washington on Thursday. Peng and Melania visited exhibition halls including the Peacock Room. Peng expressed appreciation for the US side's return of Chinese cultural relics to China on multiple occasions in recent years, expressing hope that China and the United States would continue to strengthen cooperation on cultural exchanges and cultural heritage protection, and deepen the friendship between the two peoples. After the tour, Peng and Melania watched American teenagers sing Chinese songs together and had cordial exchanges with them. Peng encouraged them to continue studying the Chinese language and culture and to become envoys of friendship between China and the United States. The National Museum of Asian Art is a renowned US institution dedicated to the collection, research and exhibition of Asian art.

item.title: FAST celebrates a decade of achievements
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-24
FAST celebrates a decade of achievements The achievements made by China's Five-hundred-meter Aperture Spherical radio Telescope, or FAST, have gained global recognition, according to senior Chinese astronomers who anticipate more breakthroughs with the telescope's upgrade. "Sensitivity is a core indicator of observational capability for radio waves. As the world's most sensitive single-dish radio telescope, FAST has an irreplaceable advantage in the field, providing a unique 'probe' for humanity to explore the universe," said Jiang Peng, chief engineer of FAST and deputy head of the National Astronomical Observatories of the Chinese Academy of Sciences. Jiang highlighted that FAST's performance has significantly exceeded initial expectations, noting that "all technical indicators have been met, and its operational efficiency and reliability are exceptional". He made these remarks on Wednesday during a three-day academic exchange event in Pingtang county, Guizhou province, celebrating the 10th anniversary of FAST's completion. The event attracted over 200 Chinese scholars from more than 40 research institutes and universities. Over the past decade, FAST has discovered over 1,300 pulsars, surpassing the total found by all other radio telescopes worldwide during the same period. It has also captured 156,000 neutral hydrogen galaxies, establishing the world's largest sample library to trace the birth and evolution of galaxies. Notably, FAST has discovered many exotic pulsars, Jiang said, including a pulsar binary with the shortest known orbital period and a pulsar-helium-star system that provides strong observational evidence for common-envelope evolution — a dramatic stellar phase in which one star engulfs its companion, ejects their shared outer layers, and leaves behind a tightly bound compact binary. "When FAST began full operations in 2020, the number of observation proposals was modest. Ten years on, demand has surged, with an annual approval rate of only 15 percent, demonstrating global recognition and our commitment to open and shared science," Jiang said. He emphasized that behind these achievements stands a dedicated team of over 100 researchers and engineers, staying true to Professor Nan Rendong's original vision of building a world-class telescope for the nation. The team has overcome pressures from construction, testing, and operation, tackling challenges such as the domestic development of high-performance steel cables and actuators, as well as the precision refinement of the measurement and control system. The team is now actively advancing Phase II of the project, which plans to deploy dozens of 40-meter-diameter antennas within a 30-kilometer radius of FAST. Once completed, this expansion is expected to double FAST's sensitivity and boost its resolution by 200 times. Earlier this year, an international research team led by Wu Xuefeng, a researcher at CAS's Purple Mountain Observatory in Nanjing, Jiangsu province, published a breakthrough in the journal Science based on FAST, providing strong evidence that at least some fast radio bursts — mysterious flashes of radio energy from deep space — are produced by compact star binaries. Like super lightning of the universe, fast radio bursts are extremely bright and transient radio phenomena, lasting only a few thousandths of a second. Wu attributed the groundbreaking discovery to the superior performance of FAST, along with its long-term monitoring and rapid response mechanisms once important abnormalities are found. "With the advancement of the second phase of the FAST project, further improvements in sensitivity will enable astronomers to contribute significantly to uncovering the ultimate question of the origin of fast radio bursts," he said, noting that the telescope has provided a platform for global leading scientists to collaborate and pursue breakthroughs in both theoretical and observational astronomy. Han Zhanwen, a CAS member and a researcher at CAS's Yunnan Observatories in Kunming, echoed Wu's views, underscoring that FAST's ultrahigh sensitivity has opened a new window for scientists, enabling the observation of many faint neutron stars and pulsars that were previously undetectable. Han emphasized that the most significant improvement in Phase II of the project is resolution. He compared the first phase project to hearing someone speaking in a room without being able to identify the speaker, whereas Phase II of the project can precisely locate the source of the sound. "This will greatly enhance the capability for multiband joint observations, allowing us to accurately identify the optical and X-ray counterparts of radio sources, thereby revealing deeper physical laws," he added. "With the advancements made by FAST, China has transitioned from being a follower to standing alongside, and now leading in the field, attracting top scientists from around the world to seek collaboration," Han said. "As Phase II of the project advances, our leading position is expected to be further consolidated."
